findings.title: Apply the consumed uncertain Task-ID fence to planned and running legacy Tasks
findings.origin: Preexisting asymmetry left uncovered by this artifact's complete consumed-effect replay scope; not represented as a newly introduced regression.
findings.criterion: HRR-SPEC criterion 2 and HRR-A require completed, consumed and uncertain occurrences to reject replay across recovery, including truthful legacy source Task coverage.
findings.evidence: In an exclusive Git fixture with an explicit continuity binding, inventory/fence uncertainEffectIds contains 'unknown'. A planned source-only Task with id 'unknown', authored nextAction 'Repeat uncertain legacy source action', and no pendingEffectIds passes validateGitWorkRecords with valid=true/findings=[]; readGitWorkContext returns source-qualified/holdReasons=[] while relevantUncertainIds=['unknown']. The equivalent completed Task-ID fence is rejected by line 870 and the existing real-source test at git-work.test.ts:1305. The pending-ID loop covers both statuses, but these legacy source Tasks deliberately have no fabricated native Effect or pendingEffectIds.
findings.impact: A recovery consumer can receive a qualified planned/running legacy source Task whose same once-only action is still uncertain. This violates the source replay hold even though the context correctly grants no native permission.
findings.requestedChange: Reject the same planned/running Task ID when it is in either consumed status set. Preserve future distinct pending effect IDs and do not invent native occurrences for source-only Tasks. Add focused uncertain source Task-ID coverage and rerun the exact successor review.
